newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia officials to meet with S.Korean merchant banks.
newsitem.headline: Kia officials to meet with S.Korean merchant banks.

text.p: South Korea's Kia Group, rocked by rumours of financial troubles, will meet merchant bankers on Thursday to try to persuade them to open credit lines to the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, a group official said.
"We will discuss various issues surrounding our group," the official said.
"We will explain our plan to sell off real estate and try to sooth jitters shared by merchant banks."
Nervous merchant banks, which have been portrayed as culprits in a series of post-Hanbo corporate failures, were blamed for calling in loans recently from the Kia Group.

The group has been rumoured to be in financial trouble for months, but speculation grew in early June when a report leaked by Samsung Motor alleged "managerial conflicts" at group flagship Kia Motors and hinted of a takeover.
Group chairman Kim Sun-hong had asked finance minister Kang Kyong-shik to persuade merchant banks to keep cash flowing to the conglomerate.
He also said the group would restructure to improve its financial status. The group will raise about 795 billion won over the next three years by selling its property holdings.

A senior official at Korea First Bank said Kia Group planned to reduce the proportion of its borrowings from merchant banks by 10 percent this year and 20 percent each in 1997 and 1998. The bank is one of Kia's major creditors.
The bank official said Kia's debts to merchant banks totalled 3.8 trillion won. But a Kia Group spokesman declined to confirm this.
